variants.title: Single-region blast radius
variants.context: An availability-zone storm takes the only region offline and the product is unreachable worldwide.
variants.constraint: RTO is 15 minutes; RPO is near-zero for orders.
variants.question: What architecture reduces that blast radius?
variants.expectedPattern: Run a second region with failover (or active-active) rather than one regional stack.
wrongChoices: A bigger VM in the same region
More disks in the failed AZ only
Client-side retries to the dead region

variants.title: DNS failover too slow
variants.context: The primary region dies, but clients cache the old IP for 30 minutes.
variants.constraint: TTL is 1800 seconds and there is no health-based routing.
variants.question: What makes regional failover actually work?
variants.expectedPattern: Health-checked global routing with short TTLs or Anycast, not static DNS alone.
wrongChoices: Hope users flush DNS
Keep a 1-hour TTL for easier caching
Failover by emailing a new URL

variants.title: Active-passive database lag
variants.context: Failover to the secondary region loses 12 minutes of orders because replication was asynchronous and unmonitored.
variants.question: What must you design and measure?
variants.expectedPattern: Replication lag SLOs, and a failover policy that matches acceptable data loss.
wrongChoices: Failover without checking lag
Synchronous cross-region commits for every analytics event
No replica in the standby region

variants.title: Users pinned to a distant region
variants.context: APAC users always hit US-East even though an APAC stack exists.
variants.question: How should traffic be steered?
variants.expectedPattern: Route users to the nearest healthy region, with failover if that region is down.
wrongChoices: One global origin for every user
Manual country files on each laptop
Force APAC through US to simplify ops

variants.title: Config deployed to one region
variants.context: A feature flag is on in EU and off in US, so checkout rules disagree.
variants.constraint: Flags must be consistent for a given user.
variants.question: What multi-region concern is this?
variants.expectedPattern: Replicate control-plane config with a defined consistency model, or pin a user to one region’s flags.
wrongChoices: Independent flags with no user affinity
Change flags only in the region that happens to be awake
Store flags in each pod’s local disk only

variants.title: Stateful sessions in one region
variants.context: Sessions live in regional memory, so a failover logs everyone out.
variants.constraint: Users must survive a region loss.
variants.question: Where should session state live?
variants.expectedPattern: Replicated or globally reachable session storage, not process memory in one region.
wrongChoices: Sticky sessions to a single region forever
No session store
Rebuild sessions only after a support ticket

variants.title: Split-brain writes
variants.context: Both regions accept order writes during a partition and two inventories diverge.
variants.question: What write policy avoids split brain?
variants.expectedPattern: A single-writer region or consensus so only one side accepts conflicting writes during a partition.
wrongChoices: Active-active writes with no conflict resolution
Last timestamp wins on money
Both regions as unconstrained primaries

variants.title: Warm standby is too cold
variants.context: The DR region has no running app instances; boot plus image pull takes 40 minutes.
variants.question: What readiness level is required?
variants.expectedPattern: A warm or hot standby with scaled-out instances already running, not a cold start.
wrongChoices: Document-only DR
One tiny VM that cannot take full load
Build AMIs after the outage starts

variants.title: Data residency vs latency
variants.context: EU user data must stay in the EU, but the only search cluster is in the US.
variants.question: How do you place the system?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep regulated data and its serving path in-region; do not replicate restricted fields globally.
wrongChoices: Copy all PII to the US for simpler search
Ignore residency because latency is worse
One global unsharded PII table

variants.title: Cron in every region
variants.context: A billing cron runs in US and EU and double-charges customers.
variants.question: How should scheduled work be coordinated?
variants.expectedPattern: Elect a single region (or a lock) for globally unique jobs; run regional jobs only on regional data.
wrongChoices: Every region runs every global job
Disable clocks
Charge twice and refund later as the design

variants.title: Object storage is regional
variants.context: Images live in one bucket; failover region 404s every avatar.
variants.constraint: The app is multi-region; the bucket is not.
variants.question: What must be replicated?
variants.expectedPattern: Replicate or dual-write blobs (or use a global namespace) so both regions can read media.
wrongChoices: Assume S3 in one region is globally durable for reads
Store images only on the app disk
Hotlink production from a laptop

variants.title: Secret rotation in one region
variants.context: API keys rotate in US and EU pods still use the old key, then auth fails after failover.
variants.constraint: Secrets must be available everywhere you might run.
variants.question: What operational pattern is required?
variants.expectedPattern: Replicate secrets and rotate with overlap so every region can authenticate during failover.
wrongChoices: Rotate in one region and fail over immediately
Hardcode keys in AMIs
Different prod keys with no mapping

variants.title: Follow-the-sun on-call vs follow-the-traffic
variants.context: Traffic is global 24/7 but only one region is staffed, so overnight incidents wait.
variants.constraint: This is an operations design issue tied to multi-region.
variants.question: What must match the architecture?
variants.expectedPattern: Runbooks, paging, and dashboards that work for every serving region, not only HQ hours.
wrongChoices: Multi-region serving with single-region observability
No paging outside HQ
Ignore secondary-region metrics

variants.title: Schema migration not dual-region
variants.context: EU is on schema v12 and US is on v11 when traffic shifts.
variants.constraint: The app cannot read the new column in the old region.
variants.question: How do you migrate a multi-region fleet?
variants.expectedPattern: Expand-contract migrations that are compatible across versions, applied in every region before cutover.
wrongChoices: Break the schema in one region first
Different schemas as a long-term state
Failover during a one-sided DDL

variants.title: Global secondary indexes lag
variants.context: A user writes in Tokyo and immediately queries a global index that is 8 seconds behind.
variants.constraint: The user expects their own write.
variants.question: What consistency rule still applies across regions?
variants.expectedPattern: Read-your-own-writes or a local index for the writer; do not pretend a lagging global index is immediate.
wrongChoices: Treat global indexes as strongly consistent everywhere
Force every read to wait for world-wide replication
Disable indexes
